title: The Lee Resolution: From Proposal to Confederation
learningObjectives: Explain how support for independence led to Richard Henry Lee proposing that the colonies be free and independent states.
Identify the three-part purpose of the Lee Resolution and the concurrent committees created to carry it out.
Describe the sequence of votes and delayed approvals from June 1776 through November 1777.

explanations.text: The Lee Resolution proposed independence, foreign alliances, and a plan for confederation, prompting Congress to create three concurrent committees to address each part.

evidence.quote: The Lee Resolution contained three parts: a declaration of independence, a call to form foreign alliances, and "a plan for confederation."
The delegates to Congress adopted strict rules of secrecy to protect the cause of American liberty and their own lives.

explanations.text: Delegates met under secrecy in Philadelphia, debated Lee's proposal, recorded the votes of twelve colonies, and later approved separate plans for treaties and confederation.

evidence.quote: Its second meeting convened in Philadelphia in 1775.
The document seen here shows the vote on the Lee Resolution — the affirmative votes of 12 colonies are listed at the right.

explanations.text: Approval of the related plans unfolded over more than a year, with the treaty plan acted on months after the Declaration and the confederation plan much later.

evidence.quote: The plan for making treaties was not approved until September of 1776;
the plan of confederation was delayed until November of 1777.

events.label: Second Continental Congress convenes in Philadelphia

evidence.quote: Its second meeting convened in Philadelphia in 1775.
The delegates to Congress adopted strict rules of secrecy to protect the cause of American liberty and their own lives.
On June 7, 1776, Richard Henry Lee of Virginia, introduced this resolution in the Second Continental Congress proposing independence for the American colonies.
The Lee Resolution contained three parts: a declaration of independence, a call to form foreign alliances, and "a plan for confederation."
On June 11, 1776, the Congress appointed three concurrent committees in response to the Lee Resolution:
"prepare and digest the form of a confederation."
New York cast no vote until the newly elected New York Convention upheld the Declaration of Independence on July 9, 1776.
The document seen here shows the vote on the Lee Resolution — the affirmative votes of 12 colonies are listed at the right.
The plan for making treaties was not approved until September of 1776;
the plan of confederation was delayed until November of 1777.
